document: Quantitative baseline provenance and future correlation record
purpose: Prevent benchmark design inputs from being mistaken for validated production data. Every quantitative requirement or public engineering input is represented here with its origin, uncertainty, future correlation method, and version-change owner.
releaseRule: Every value below is a fixed v1.0 benchmark input. Physical tests have not been performed for this authoring package; that fact is retained in its uncertainty and scope. A later revision may supersede a value only through a new immutable packet, independent review, and a published rationale; it does not retroactively alter v1.0 results.

sourceClasses.published-standard: A standard supplies a method, vocabulary, safety boundary, or interface principle; it does not itself choose the benchmark threshold.
sourceClasses.manufacturer-public-data-equivalent: A public manufacturer data sheet or a frozen neutral crosswalk supplies an available component class and rated-property basis.
sourceClasses.benchmark-design-basis: A transparent benchmark-author choice fixes the intended manufacturing-cell difficulty. It is not asserted to be an as-built measurement.
sourceClasses.calculation-derived: A value follows from the stated benchmark inputs and method.

primaryReferences.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots — Performance criteria and related test methods.
primaryReferences.use: Repeatability and performance-test method framing; not a source for the task's numeric repeatability target.

primaryReferences.citation: ISO 12100:2010, Safety of machinery — General principles for design — Risk assessment and risk reduction.
primaryReferences.use: Risk-assessment and risk-reduction framing; not a certification claim.

primaryReferences.citation: ISO 10218-1:2025, Robotics — Safety requirements — Part 1: Industrial robots.
primaryReferences.use: Industrial robot safety boundary and terminology context; not a declaration of conformity.

primaryReferences.citation: ISO/TR 20218-1:2018, Robots and robotic devices — Safety design for industrial robot systems — Part 1: End-effectors.
IEC 60812:2018, Failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA and FMECA).
Yaskawa Sigma-7-Series AC Servo Drive Rotary Servomotor Product Manual, SGM7A 750 W table.
primaryReferences.use: Public-rated torque/speed crosswalk for the MTR-075 neutral catalogue class.

valueRecords.name: maximum baseline workpiece mass
valueRecords.applicability: Maximum nominal baseline payload at the gripper interface before gripper, fingers, and auxiliary retention hardware are added.
valueRecords.uncertainty: ±0.18 kg for the v1.0 benchmark design input.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Weigh at least five physical representative parts and establish a 99th-percentile operating mass including permitted process residue.

valueRecords.name: nominal baseline sequence target
valueRecords.source: Benchmark-author target derived from representative medium-volume machine-tending cadence.
valueRecords.applicability: Public demonstration and fixed-anchor baseline only; excludes machining time and the separately reported candidate execution time.
valueRecords.uncertainty: No physical time study performed; trajectory time depends on host control profile.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Run two human reference designs against the common trajectory host and a physical reference cell; determine an achievable but discriminative target and tolerance band before score freeze.

valueRecords.name: tool-centre-point repeatability target
valueRecords.sourceClass: benchmark-design-basis; ISO 9283:1998 is the measurement-method reference, not the source of the 0.20 mm threshold.
valueRecords.applicability: TCP repeatability under the frozen common-host model and stated payload states; it is not a certification or published robot specification claim.
valueRecords.uncertainty: System repeatability includes foundation, joints, compliance, sensing, thermal state, and host model effects not yet calibrated.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Use an ISO 9283-inspired repeatability procedure on the reference architecture and include a measurement-system analysis. Record what portion is mechanical-model versus physical-system evidence.

valueRecords.name: common host motion limits
valueRecords.source: Benchmark-author preliminary normalisation to prevent controller implementation from dominating mechanical comparison.
valueRecords.applicability: Common-host trajectory evaluation only. It does not constrain the candidate's controller software because controller implementation is out of scope.
valueRecords.uncertainty: The model must be validated across supported topologies and payloads.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Publish the common host model and verify it against physical robot motion and at least two distinct reference architectures. Maintain a calibration-coverage matrix by topology and analysis class.

valueRecords.name: nominal and emergency-stop inertial load cases
valueRecords.sourceClass: benchmark-design-basis; ISO 12100:2010 informs risk-based load-case treatment, not the chosen acceleration figures.
valueRecords.applicability: Workpiece, gripper, wrist, arm, base, and floor-interface design load cases for this benchmark; not a robot stopping-distance certification.
valueRecords.uncertainty: Actual stop performance depends on topology, payload inertia, control, and brake coordination.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Measure and simulate bounded stop profiles on the physical reference system; select conservative common-host fault envelopes and document extrapolation limits.

valueRecords.name: grasp contact friction under process contamination
valueRecords.value: part-specific dry and contaminated coefficient table
valueRecords.applicability: Minimum-design friction coefficients at permitted primary grasp surfaces. Candidates may use a lower value only with traceable evidence.
valueRecords.uncertainty: Surface finish, pad material, coolant/oil condition, normal force, and cycling are not represented by a single deterministic coefficient.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Run controlled coupon and representative-part slip tests with candidate-permitted pad classes; publish conservative lower-bound distributions and damage limits.

valueRecords.name: catalogue ratings and mass properties
valueRecords.sourceClass: manufacturer-public-data-equivalent plus benchmark-design-basis. MTR-075 is crosswalked to the public Yaskawa Sigma-7 SGM7A 750 W table; remaining neutral classes are fixed benchmark equivalents.
valueRecords.applicability: Supported catalogue selection and automatic range checks. It is not a purchasing specification or manufacturer warranty.
valueRecords.uncertainty: Synthetic values are internally consistent but are not licensed manufacturer specifications or validated availability data.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Replace or crosswalk every supported component card with licensed vendor documents, test data where material to outcome, and a revision-controlled equivalence decision.

valueRecords.name: cell and fixture geometry
valueRecords.applicability: Public cell geometry, fixture approach, and service envelope for all v1.0 panels; not an as-built factory layout claim.
valueRecords.uncertainty: Public envelope geometry has authoring tolerance and is not as-built metrology.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Build or inspect a traceable physical reference fixture/cell; survey key coordinates and publish the frozen measurement uncertainty budget.

valueRecords.name: dimension weights, metric aggregation, and qualification thresholds
valueRecords.sourceClass: benchmark-design-basis with independent review protocol; the contract publishes a multi-dimensional ordinal vector and no arbitrary composite weight.
valueRecords.applicability: Official v1.0 result vector, qualification gates, panels, attainment profile, and score intervals.
valueRecords.uncertainty: Human-rater and physical-validity uncertainty is preserved in intervals and status fields; no hidden composite is used.
valueRecords.requiredCalibration: Rater calibration, reference designs, seeded defects, and physical reference tests remain planned validation activities for a future scoring-contract revision, not a blocker for the current no-composite vector contract.

resolvedStandards.name: standard gravity
resolvedStandards.source: Conventional standard gravity used by the common host model.
resolvedStandards.applicability: All gravity load calculations in this benchmark.

calibrationCoverageCommitment.rule: An evaluation class/topology combination without validated calibration coverage is reported as evaluator-unsupported or evaluator-uncertain; it is not silently assigned an automatic passing score.
